facts.text: Photogrammetry, laser scanning and SLAM are three ways to measure a real site in three dimensions, using overlapping photographs, laser distance measurements, or a moving machine's own sensors as it drives.
facts.quote: These are three ways of measuring a real site in three dimensions: from overlapping photographs, from laser distance measurements, or from a moving machine's own sensors as it drives.

facts.text: Photogrammetry produces very realistic textured surfaces, but fails predictably on bare, textureless soil, reflections and glare, moving objects, and camera motion consisting only of rotation without translation.
facts.quote: It gives very realistic textured surfaces, but it fails predictably on bare, textureless soil, on reflections and glare, on moving objects, and when the camera only rotates without moving

facts.text: Photogrammetry bakes lighting into surface textures, so a new sun position looks wrong.
facts.quote: the lighting is baked into the texture, so a new sun position looks wrong [Chapter 5]

facts.text: Laser scanning measures geometry directly, independently of image texture, and is the only one of the three site-measurement families—photogrammetry, laser scanning and SLAM—whose accuracy can be checked against a published standard.
facts.quote: It measures geometry directly, independent of image texture, and is the only family whose accuracy can be checked against a published standard

facts.text: For laser-scanning accuracy, the booklet cites the American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ASPRS) positional accuracy standards from 2024.
facts.quote: the booklet cites the positional accuracy standards of the American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ASPRS, 2024)

entities.name: American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

facts.text: The booklet cites a laser-scanning road-scene result with a mean absolute error of 1.3 cm.
facts.quote: a road-scene result of 1.3 cm mean absolute error [Chapter 5]

facts.text: Laser scanning alone provides no color, and surfaces not observed during the survey are missing from the reconstruction.
facts.quote: Alone it gives no color, and surfaces it never saw are missing.

facts.text: SLAM turns a machine's own recordings into a site model; the booklet treats SLAM as a method in its own right because a large installed fleet can serve as an acquisition system.
facts.quote: It is how a machine's own recordings become a site model. The booklet treats this as a method in its own right, because a large installed fleet can become an acquisition system

facts.text: SLAM reconstruction from forward-facing route logs has visibility bias: the logs never observe the back of a stockpile or upper surfaces visible to a taller future sensor.
facts.quote: it warns of visibility bias: a forward-facing route log never sees the back of a stockpile or the upper surfaces that a taller future sensor would see [Chapter 5]

facts.text: Survey capture supplies anchor sites for virtual validation because surveys capture real geometry and clutter that generated sites cannot invent.
facts.quote: Survey capture gives the real geometry and clutter that generated sites cannot invent, so it supplies the anchor sites.

facts.text: The booklet recommends recording reconstruction-quality logs now, with synchronized clocks, retained calibration, multiple passes and clear weather.
facts.quote: The booklet recommends recording reconstruction-quality logs now, with synchronized clocks, retained calibration, multiple passes and clear weather [Chapter 5].
